text:
Pierre-Luc Dubois has played 11 of Washington's games and the Capitals look different when he does. With him on the ice at 5v5 they have 59% of expected goals (the quality of chances), more than seven points better than without him. Ten points, seven of them assists, none on the power play.

That is the most encouraging part. His points are coming at even strength, against strong competition (Evolving-Hockey had his opponents in the 98th percentile last season), and he set up teammates more than he shot. He scored in each of his last two games, including the winner against Florida.

There is some air in it. His points per 60 are running above his usual range, and the on-ice shooting with him out there has been kind. Expect the pace to settle closer to the middle of his range rather than the top.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 71% of his entries last season, a small sample of seven games. The thing to watch is whether he stays in the lineup: he missed a stretch of October games.
headline: Dubois tilts the ice when he plays
